title: Ontario Reformatory heritage district plan amended
subtitle: Also: Official Plan update approved, Niska parkland redesignation directed, heritage notice, and corrected remuneration vote records.
overview: Council's main debate was the Ontario Reformatory Heritage Conservation District. Council voted to designate the district but amended the plan to remove mentions and provisions for residential development {{vote:m5}}. Staff will bring the revised plan and by-law back to a future meeting, with staff saying that would be in the second quarter. Staff had argued residential policies would give the City more heritage tools if the province sold the land. Delegates and several councillors said they signal support for housing on the site.

Council approved Official Plan Amendment 110, a first-phase update that brings the Official Plan in line with provincial changes and City master plans {{vote:m7}}. It directed staff to report back by the second quarter of 2026 with an Official Plan and zoning amendment designating a parcel of the Niska/Courtright lands as open space and parkland {{vote:m8}}. Staff said an earlier April date would not be manageable.

Council also began the heritage designation process for 44 Edinburgh Road North through the consent agenda. It corrected how votes on the Council Remuneration Review were recorded in the February 3 draft minutes {{vote:m10}}. After a closed session on zoning by-law appeals at the Ontario Land Tribunal, the Mayor reported that Council gave direction to staff.

decisions.detail: Council approved designating the district as amended, directing staff to remove residential development provisions from the plan and bring the revised plan and by-law back for approval {{vote:m6}}.

decisions.item: Removing residential from the heritage plan
decisions.detail: Council amended the plan so that mentions and provisions for residential development are removed {{vote:m5}}.
Council approved the City-initiated Phase 1 Official Plan update, which aligns the plan with provincial and municipal changes {{vote:m7}}.
Staff must report back by Q2 2026 with an Official Plan and zoning amendment designating the identified parcel as open space and parkland {{vote:m8}}.
The City Clerk was authorized to publish and serve notice of intention to designate the property under the Ontario Heritage Act {{vote:m3}}.
The Clerk was directed to correct the February 3 Committee of the Whole draft minutes to show how four members voted on the Council Remuneration Review clauses {{vote:m10}}.

debate: Delegates and some councillors argued that listing residential use in the heritage plan signals support for housing on the site and could constrain later decisions. They said land use changes should go through public planning processes instead.

Staff said the plan only contemplates residential use and gives no permission for it. Without those policies, a provincial zoning order or sale could leave the City with fewer heritage tools in the area where buildings are unused.

Several delegates urged moving the Niska lands redesignation up to April 2026, citing risk to the land and public funds used to buy it. The Mayor and the CAO said April was not manageable and that the planning process includes public engagement.

On the Official Plan update, delegates asked whether the parkland shortfall estimate had been updated and raised water supply concerns. Staff said a parkland acquisition strategy is planned for 2027. The CAO said water and wastewater capacity is planned to 2051.
A delegate asked that Council wait on Official Plan Amendment 110 until a site-specific redesignation was considered. Staff asked Council to keep site-specific matters separate from the update.
